demonstration.profile: Calm water, default boat; one suitable example, not universal seamanship

units.heading: rad clockwise from north
units.lineTension: N; modeled planar spring/damper load, not measured rope safe working load
units.lineLength: m (planar); rest length includes attachment slack
units.estimatedPeakLoadN: N = summed tick normal impulse / fixed dt; NOT physical peak force or damage

data.explanation: Equal engine settings keep the bow north. Watch SOG: momentum builds gradually, so avoid carrying full power toward the berth.
Neutral alone does not stop the boat. Use short, equal reverse bursts when needed, then return to neutral as speed falls.
Hold low speed and heading in the mint approach target for three seconds. This unlocks line attachment; it is not yet a secured berth.

events.message: Berth held — attach bow and stern lines

data.explanation: For this calm, aligned example we choose bow → B01 first. This is not a universal order: wind, current and the end drifting away can change the priority. The first line activates the amber alongside area.

events.message: First line attached — amber alongside envelope replaces the approach target

data.explanation: Attach stern → B02 within reach and at low speed. Each line initially has slack. Attachment neither stops the boat instantly nor moves it into position.
Take in short lengths on both lines to draw the boat toward the quay without twisting it unnecessarily. Lines only pull. Watch load and movement; Ease pays line out if more length is needed.
Both engines remain neutral. Check the amber envelope, parallel heading, low movement, fenders, and both lines with limited slack and safe loads. Gentle covered fender contact is allowed.

events.message: Secured: both lines, starboard fenders and neutral held for 3s — simulation remains live

data.explanation: The ordinary securing checks passed. The lesson is now paused. Take over to practise, repeat the example, or return to your unchanged practice attempt. This two-line game example is not a complete real-world mooring procedure.

events.message: Secured conditions lost — tend lines and regain the berth
